To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the database scheme obtained through the exhaustive application of the scheme operations is the optimal database scheme, and that the retrieval on the original scheme is equivalent to the retrieval on the new scheme.

the two scheme operations, merge, which merges two relation schemes, and copy, which copies a functional dependency from a relation scheme to one of its tightly related relation schemes, are sufficient to obtain an optimal database scheme for a class of routine activities whose access patterns remain fixed.

(1) the two scheme operations can be applied to a database scheme without introducing anomalies, and (2) if the conditions for applying the scheme operations are satisfied, then the database scheme is optimal and the view of a retrieval is equivalent to that on the original database.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a database design method for efficient query processing.
a database scheme design method to improve query processing efficiency by reducing the number of joins.

the problem of finding an optimal database scheme for the class of database activities whose access pattern is fixed, and the problem of finding the equivalent views for the activities on the original and the new databases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a database scheme obtained by applying the scheme operations to a given database scheme as long as the necessary conditions are satisfied, is optimal in terms of the number of joins required to retrieve the data.

, given a class of database activities with fixed access patterns, the database scheme which is obtained by exhaustive applications to the original scheme of these scheme operations as long as no anomalies are caused, is optimal in that no further applications of one of these operations can avoid anomalies and that no further applications to the new scheme of one of these scheme operations can avoid anomalies.

the scheme obtained by applying the scheme operations exhaustively as long as the necessary and sufficient conditions hold, is the optimal scheme in that it has the minimum number of joins in the retrieval of any database activity in a class of routine ones whose access patterns are given.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a systematic approach for designing database schemes for efficient query processing.
the scheme transformation operations are useful to improve performance of database systems, while the conditions for applying these operations are necessary to avoid anomalies.

, in order to reduce the number, and thus to improve the efficiency, of joins in a class of routine queries, the relational database scheme should be designed so that all the relations are tightly related and the functional dependencies are copied to the tightly related relations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the database scheme obtained from an initial scheme by applying these operations is optimal in the above sense, and that the view of a retrieval query on the original database is the same as that on the new database.
the number of join operations can be reduced by applying merge and copy operations.
the database designer should consider not only the database scheme, but also the retrieval scheme in the design process of relational database systems.
